content.key_idea: Habitus splits work across a thin client (feature/pose collection, frame buffering) and an edge host that predicts mmWave throughput and schedules content delivery across 802.11ac/ad links, proxying between the client and the content server.
content.reading_order: Left to right: a pre-trained model feeds the Edge's throughput predictor alongside the pose estimator, whose outputs drive the Multipath Scheduler delivering content to the Client on the right.

summary: Habitus is a software framework that helps immersive content delivery apps exploit heterogeneous wireless links via mmWave throughput prediction and multipath networking. Figure 2 shows its architecture as an Edge/Client split: on the client, a Feature Collector gathers real-time signals (e.g. the headset's 6-DoF pose and network info) and forwards them to the Edge, while a Frame Buffer holds received content. On the edge -- where all components but the client-side collector reside -- a Full-body Pose Estimator and a Throughput Predictor (an online-transfer-learning model seeded by an offline Pre-trained Model) inform a Multipath Scheduler that splits delivery across an omnidirectional 802.11ac link and an mmWave 802.11ad link. The edge also proxies between the client and an external Content Server, forwarding requests and streamed content. The diagram is icon-heavy line art with no fill color, using dashed versus solid lines to separate control data from content data.

notes: The sentence describing what uses the throughput-prediction results is truncated ('...utilized by the ap-'), and the retrieved text does not detail how the Full-body Pose Estimator interacts with the Throughput Predictor/Multipath Scheduler internally, so some intra-Edge flows are read from the figure's layout alone. layout-proposal: edge-mediated host-device — an Edge host (pose estimation, throughput prediction, multipath scheduling) sits between a thin Client device and an upstream Content Server, proxying both control and content data over two wireless links; host-device is the closest named template for the Edge/Client pair but does not capture the added Content Server node.
